messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: Inference error rate spike (>5%) observed for us-east-1a model-serving cluster rwd-infer-prod. Auto-alert triggered.
jamie: seeing increased 502/504 from frontend gateways, spike started ~3490012300.
sarah: digging into control plane — our resolvers returning stale egress IPs due to TTL mismatch; some responses still point to decommissioned NAT IPs.
leo: host metrics on nodes in us-east-1a show RX errors and conn resets, consistent with egress path failures.
tess: customers seeing intermittent failures, some requests eventually succeed after retries; SLO window entering breach at 3490012600.
jamie: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) divert traffic off us-east-1a to us-east-1b, 2) restart edge proxy pods to clear DNS caches, 3) push resolver-priority change to prefer healthy resolvers.
sarah: applying routing policy now to shift endpoints 30% -> 70% -> 100% to us-east-1b, will monitor error rate. Link to routing UI: https://console.redwood/routing/cluster/rwd-infer-prod
incident-bot: ACTION: routing-policy change initiated by sarah at 3490012380
leo: rolling restart of edge-proxy started (kubectl rollout restart deployment/edge-proxy -n inference). Adding postStart to flush local nscd.
tess: starting canary traffic shift: 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Monitoring 5xx, latency, token throughput.
oncall: taking pager, staying on until handoff at 3490013000. Will own immediate comms.
sarah: found resolver cluster with stale glue/primed entries — escalated to cloud provider resolver team, opened ticket.
jamie: temporary workaround: apply TTL override on our side to 30s for affected zones; will force caches to refresh in ~2x TTL window.
leo: flushed conntrack on impacted nodes to clear half-open conn states: sudo conntrack -F executed via SSH job.
tess: drafted customer notice: short explanation + remediation steps, low blast radius recommendation, internal status posted.
oncall: following runbook steps: dns-flush, reroute, canary, restart proxies, escalate to provider. All steps in progress.
incident-bot: NOTE: SLO alert suppressed for region failover during mitigation window (suppression id s-349001).
sarah: provider acknowledged issue — their resolver cache incorrectly primed entries, they are expiring and returning correct egress IPs now.
jamie: monitoring metrics — will consider rolling back routing policy when error rate <1% for 10m.
tess: current readouts: error rate dropped 6.3% -> 0.8% in canary, 95th latency unchanged.
oncall: handing initial shift to jamie for cleanup and postmortem run; handoff at 3490013000 :wave:
jamie: will stay on for 2hr observation window, will open postmortem with timeline and root cause analysis once stable.
sarah: postmortem notes: add TTL drift monitor, avoid long TTLs for zones referencing dynamic NAT pools, add proactive resolver consistency checks.
leo: commands used for mitigation saved for postmortem:
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/edge-proxy -n inference
for node in $(kubectl get nodes -l az=us-east-1a -o name); do ssh $node -- sudo conntrack -F; done
resolvectl flush-caches || sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches
```
tess: tagging impacted customers and updating incident doc with timeline + followups.
jamie: marking incident as mitigated for now. Will re-open paging if regressions appear. Thanks team :thumbsup:
